title: Schur-certified two-scale semigroup budget for the intrinsic graph
question: Can the late-time IR leg of the R-414 semigroup criterion use the conservative harmonic/Schur gap from R-406, so that coarse inter-phase capacity and block-mean-zero residual coercivity are explicit inputs to the Green-trace budget?
method: Rebuild the R-406 conditional graph, phase block partition, harmonic extension and Schur/residual gaps on every declared finite row.
Check the finite variational relation kappa_S=half min(kappa_coarse,kappa_residual)<=lambda_1 before using the certified gap in a semigroup envelope.
Enumerate all R-412 mixed exponent profiles and retain the R-414 short-time UV power budget.
Check the late exponential envelope and integrated Green-trace criterion with kappa_S, recording coarse and residual gaps separately.
Repeat the complete finite grid in an independent plain-loop implementation and apply omission, wrong-gap, wrong-shift, time-order, sign and alpha=1 hostile mutations.
Compile the scalar positivity and finite-scope bookkeeping lemmas in Lean R415.
finding: The primary lane passes 10440/10440 assertions over 8 systems, 80 Gibbs/orientation profiles and 1030 conditional rows. The independent lane passes 10439/10439 on the same grid, the hostile lane passes 9/9, the integrated verifier passes 50/50, and Lean R415 compiles. The primary certified Schur gap range is [0.3172951609382775,3.232260013170645], the first-positive gap range is [0.6310329497027756,6.229495058532403], the split heat range is [0.001995374453234255,0.5926882083380163], the minimum Green-trace slack is 2.8762895669125346, and the maximum Mellin residual is 4.996003610813204e-16.
decision_reason: Replacing the late black-box eigenvalue by the conservative R-406 Schur certificate makes coarse inter-phase capacity and block-mean-zero residual coercivity auditable inside the same proper-time budget. The finite bridge advances the interface toward broken-sector GNS coercivity, while every regulator-independent premise remains open.

adversarial_review.check: Using a larger unverified gap gives a late-budget deficit 2.920502936517768.
Omitting the finite IR head gives a short-budget deficit 0.11755608825868386.
Omitting the UV integral term gives a short-budget deficit 0.13507226908622838.
Dropping H(tau)/kappa_S gives a Green deficit 0.4775461490944841.
Using the wrong exponential time origin gives a deficit 2.7432509056332397.
Changing the split sign leaves residual 6.239564084015606.
alpha=1 is rejected before an integral budget is formed.
Finite Schur positivity does not imply cutoff/volume/source/phase/exhaustion uniformity, a common core, GNS coercivity, a physical gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.

qft_interface.closed: Finite Schur-certified late semigroup envelope, short-time UV power budget, integrated Green-trace criterion, full row coverage, hostile shortcut rejection and Lean scalar bookkeeping.
qft_interface.open: Uniform Schur coarse/residual bounds, a common split and heat value on one Hamiltonian core, phase-boundary identification, R-399 shell transfer, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, continuum and physical-gap obligations.

next_action: Prove source/cutoff/volume/phase/exhaustion-uniform lower bounds for both Schur components and the split heat on one Hamiltonian common core; identify the coarse phase boundary; transfer the two-scale budget to the R-399 shell. If either component collapses under validated growing stress, retain only the finite diagnostic and record the obstruction.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite Schur-certified two-scale semigroup bridge only. It proves no cutoff-, volume-, source-, phase- or exhaustion-uniform gap or UV coefficient, common core, phase selection, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: The R-406 harmonic/Schur lower bound supplies a conservative finite IR input for the R-414 heat budget and exposes the phase-capacity route; it does not supply regulator-independent coercivity or a physical-sector conclusion.
